name: KOTO
summary: KOTO is based at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility, Tokai. It studies rare neutral-kaon decays. X⁰ denotes a hypothetical invisible particle, rather than established dark matter.
detection_principle: A CsI calorimeter reconstructs π⁰→γγ, requires no additional visible activity and uses transverse momentum and decay vertices to search for KL→π⁰ plus an invisible final state.

results.summary: No candidate in the KL→π⁰νν signal region; an invisible X⁰ of 135 MeV/c² is constrained to BR(KL→π⁰X⁰)<2.4×10⁻⁹ (90% CL).

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
